A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same AirSplat research. Their complete main texts and appendices, including equations, tables, and figures, are readable and support reliable comparison after matching relocated and renumbered content.

before.justification: v1 reports original NVS experiments on RE10K, DL3DV, and ACID, component ablations, 7-Scenes geometry evaluation, and training-time measurements.

after.justification: v2 retains those empirical results and additionally reports AirSplat adaptations of SPFSplat and WorldMirror and training-memory measurements.

M1.justification: The SCPA procedure, ROM formulation, spatial regularization, and overall training objective remain unchanged. Applying the framework to additional backbones and clarifying the teacher's pose inputs do not establish a revised algorithm.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate NVS on RE10K, DL3DV, and ACID and geometry estimation on 7-Scenes. The additional backbone experiments use the existing 24-view RE10K setting. Dynamic scenes, larger view counts, and robotics are discussed as limitations or future work, not newly evaluated coverage.

E2.justification: The existing benchmark comparator sets are retained. New Appendix C/Table 5 expands the evaluated method variants by comparing SPFSplat and WorldMirror with and without AirSplat, alongside DA3; the original baseline families already appeared in v1.

E3.justification: v2 adds evaluations using SPFSplat and WorldMirror as fine-tuned backbones and adds peak training memory to Table 4. Appendix B revises the reported stability constant from 10^-7 to 10^-8, matching Section 3.3 in both versions; this does not establish that experiments were rerun. Existing splits, resolutions, and training budgets remain unchanged.

E4.justification: New Appendix C tests whether AirSplat's benefits transfer beyond DA3 to two other backbones in one retained evaluation setting. Table 4 adds memory-cost comparisons across training variants. Existing component ablations, pose-drift examples, and training-time analysis are retained.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run counts, seeds, confidence intervals, error bars, or significance tests. The existing means and medians for geometry metrics retain the same reporting practice.

E6.justification: New Table 5 reports 24-view RE10K PSNR of 22.76 for SPFSplat+AirSplat and 23.66 for WorldMirror+AirSplat, compared with their unadapted scores of 21.32 and 21.08. Table 4 adds memory measurements, including 30.56 GB for the full model. Previously reported benchmark, ablation, geometry, and timing values remain unchanged.

T1.justification: The mathematical definitions and derivations in Equations 1–10 are retained. No theorem, proof, or formal assumption is added or revised; the appendix's decay-rate symbol correction does not change the mathematics.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction's contribution list, and conclusion retain the same claims about SCPA, ROM, improved pose-free NVS, and preservation of geometric priors. Additional backbone results support these claims without redefining the central contributions.

C2.justification: The existing occlusion limitation moves from Appendix G to Section 5, which additionally identifies scaling costs and degradation on moving or inconsistent scenes. Appendix C interprets larger adaptation gains for 3D-VS-VFMs, while new Appendix I discusses dynamic reconstruction, higher-resolution inputs, and possible robotics and multimodal applications.

D1.justification: Appendix B newly specifies that the teacher uses context poses predicted by the framework. It corrects the stability constant and decay-rate notation. Table 4 clarifies that the ROM variant includes context-target training and documents GPU memory. Optimizer, hardware, training duration, and project-access information remain unchanged.

R1.justification: Section 2.1 adds discussion of InstantSplat, QuickSplat, and DAPS-AGF, distinguishing accelerated per-scene refinement from feed-forward reconstruction. Appendix I adds references supporting proposed future directions. These are focused extensions; the central research positioning remains intact.

P1.justification: v2 makes localized grammar, spelling, terminology, and affiliation edits. It relocates and expands limitations, adds acknowledgements and appendix sections on additional baselines and future work, and updates cross-references. Most existing prose and the main narrative structure are retained.

P2.justification: v2 adds the backbone-comparison Table 5, expands Table 4 with a GPU-memory column and clearer row labels, and revises Figure 1's caption. Existing qualitative panels are retained, while appendix tables and figures are renumbered or repositioned through layout reflow.

improvement.justification: v2 strengthens evidence that the training framework transfers beyond DA3 and makes memory costs, teacher-pose inputs, and applicability limits clearer. It also resolves an appendix hyperparameter inconsistency. These improve evidential support and reproducibility, while the unchanged method and existing results make the overall improvement limited.
